parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Determine the SI base units of the moment of a force.

markscheme_points.text: base units: kg m s^-2 x m = kg m^2 s^-2

hints: Hint 1: Think about what you multiply together to get a moment, and then break each of those quantities down into its fundamental kg, m and s building blocks.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Break the moment into its parts**
Think of a moment as a turning effect. It comes from a force multiplied by a distance from the pivot: $$ \text{moment} = F \times d $$ So its units must be the units of force multiplied by the units of distance.

Step 2: **Convert to base units**
Force in newtons has base units $$ 1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2} $$ Multiply by a distance in metres, $\text{m}$: $$ \text{unit of moment} = \text{kg m s}^{-2} \times \text{m} = \text{kg m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2} $$

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem:
A uniform square sheet of card $ABCD$ is freely pivoted by a pin at a point $P$. The card is held in a vertical plane by an external force in the position shown in Fig. 1.1.

{{figure:figure_1_1}}

Fig. 1.1 (not to scale)

The card has weight $0.15\text{ N}$ which may be considered to act at the centre of gravity $G$. Each side of the card has length $17\text{ cm}$. Point $P$ lies on the horizontal line $AC$ and is $4.0\text{ cm}$ from corner $A$. Line $BD$ is vertical.

The card is released by removing the external force. The card then swings in a vertical plane until it comes to rest.
parts.text: Calculate the magnitude of the resultant moment about point $P$ acting on the card immediately after it is released.

markscheme_points.text: distance of COG from P (= GP) = 17 cos 45° - 4.0 or (144.5)1/2 - 4.0 (= 8.0 cm)

hints: Hint 1: The whole weight of 0.15 N acts straight down at G. For the turning effect about P, focus on the horizontal separation between the vertical line through G and the pivot P in Fig. 1.1.
Hint 2: First find the full distance AG from the 17 cm side and the 45 degree angle, then subtract the 4.0 cm AP to get the moment arm. Remember to convert cm to m before multiplying by weight.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Picture the turning effect**
The weight $0.15 \text{ N}$ acts vertically down at G. The pivot is at P, to the left of G. That offset means the weight will try to rotate the card about P. The moment arm is the horizontal distance PG, the perpendicular distance from P to the line of action of the weight.

Step 2: **Find the distance PG**
G is the centre of the square, so AG is half the diagonal AC. From triangle with side $17 \text{ cm}$ at $45^{\circ}$: $$ AG = 17 \cos 45^{\circ} \approx 12.0 \text{ cm} $$ P is $4.0 \text{ cm}$ from A along the same line, so: $$ PG = AG - AP = 17 \cos 45^{\circ} - 4.0 \approx 8.0 \text{ cm} = 0.080 \text{ m} $$

Step 3: **Calculate the moment**
Now multiply force by perpendicular distance: $$ \text{moment} = W \times PG = 0.15 \times 0.080 $$ $$ \text{moment} = 1.2 \times 10^{-2} \text{ N m} $$ This is the resultant moment about P just after release, because the pin force at P has no moment about P.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why, when the card has come to rest, its centre of gravity is vertically below point $P$.

markscheme_points.text: (line of action of) weight acts through pivot/P or distance between (line of action of) weight and pivot/P is zero
(so) weight does not have a moment about pivot/P

hints: Hint 1: When the card finally stops swinging, there is no longer any turning effect. Think about what that tells you about the resultant moment about P.
Hint 2: A force can only cause a moment if its line of action misses the pivot. Think about where the vertical line through G must lie relative to P for its moment to be zero.
parts.proper_answer: When at rest the resultant moment about P is zero. The line of action of the weight passes through P, so the perpendicular distance is zero and the weight has no moment about P.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Rest means balanced turning**
While swinging, the offset weight creates a moment that rotates the card back toward equilibrium. For the card to stay at rest, the resultant moment about P must be zero. Otherwise it would start turning again.

Step 2: **Why G must be under P**
The only forces with a possible moment about P are the weight at G, since the contact force at the pin P acts at the pivot. Moment is force times perpendicular distance: $$ \text{moment} = W \times \text{perpendicular distance} $$ The only way this can be zero with a non-zero weight is if the perpendicular distance is zero. That happens when the vertical line of action of the weight passes straight through P. For stable rest, G hangs vertically below P.
